text.K-2: Hi {name}! This is **Wilmington**, a real town in Ohio. Let's explore!
text.3-5: Hi {name}! Welcome to **Wilmington**, Ohio. Every building, road and tree here comes from real map data.
text.6-8: Hi {name}. This is a 3D model of **Wilmington**, Ohio, built from real map data: every building, road and creek.
text.9-12: Hi {name}. This is a 3D model of **Wilmington**, Ohio, built from open map data. Footprints are real; heights are exaggerated 3x.

text.K-2: A **data center** is a big building. What do you think is inside?
text.3-5: Towns are being asked to build **data centers**. What do you think is inside one?
text.6-8: A **data center** is a large building. What do you think fills most of it?
text.9-12: Companies want to build **data centers** in towns like this. What fills most of the building?

right.K-2: Yes! It's full of **computers**. They keep videos, games and photos.
right.3-5: Yes! It's full of **computers** that store videos, games and messages for the internet.
right.6-8: Right: thousands of **servers** that store and process data for apps and websites.
right.9-12: Correct: rows of **servers** that store and process data for cloud services and AI.

wrong.K-2: Good guess! It's really full of **computers**. They keep videos, games and photos.
wrong.3-5: Good guess! It's really full of **computers** that store videos, games and messages.
wrong.6-8: Not quite: it's mostly **servers** that store and process data for apps and websites.
wrong.9-12: Not quite: it's mostly **servers** that store and process data for cloud services and AI.

text.K-2: When you watch a video, a computer in a **data center** sends it to you!
text.3-5: When you watch a video or play online, a **data center** far away is doing the work.
text.6-8: Streaming, searching and messaging all run on **data centers**, often hundreds of miles away.
text.9-12: "The cloud" is physical: **data centers** full of servers, connected by fiber and powered by the grid.

text.K-2: Let's build one! Drag the **Enterprise** card onto the glowing square.
text.3-5: Let's build one! Drag the **Enterprise** card onto the glowing square.
text.6-8: Build one: drag the **Enterprise** data center onto open land outside town.
text.9-12: Site one: drag the **Enterprise** data center onto open land outside town.

doneText.3-5: You built it! It covers 80 acres, about as big as 60 football fields.
doneText.6-8: Placed! The site is 80 acres, about 60 football fields.
doneText.9-12: Placed. The site is 80 acres, about 60 football fields.

text.K-2: See the **cranes**? Builders are still making it.
text.3-5: See the **cranes** and steel frames? It takes about two years to build.
text.6-8: It's still **under construction**: steel frames and cranes. Big ones take years to build.
text.9-12: It's **under construction**. Large sites are built in phases over several years.

text.K-2: Computers need **electricity**. How many homes use as much as this data center?
text.3-5: This data center uses **{mw} megawatts** of power. How many homes use that much electricity?
text.6-8: It draws **{mw} MW**. If it runs at full power all year, how many homes' worth of electricity is that?
text.9-12: At **{mw} MW**, running at full power all year, it uses {mwh} MWh. About how many homes use that much?

text.K-2: Let's finish building it! Drag the **year slider** to 2027.
text.3-5: Let's finish building it. Drag the **year slider** to 2027, when it opens.
text.6-8: Move the **year slider** to 2027, when it opens.
text.9-12: Advance the **year slider** to 2027, when it comes online.

text.K-2: Computers get **hot**! The circles on the roof are big **fans** that cool them.
text.3-5: Computers make lots of **heat**. The circles on the roof are giant **fans** that keep them cool.
text.6-8: Almost all the electricity turns into **heat**. Rooftop fans and cooling systems carry it away.
text.9-12: Nearly every watt a server uses becomes **heat**, so cooling is a big part of a data center's design.

right.K-2: You got it! It uses as much electricity as about **{homes} homes**. That's a whole city!
right.3-5: You got it! It uses as much electricity as about **{homes} homes**.
right.6-8: Correct: if it runs at full power all year, that's as much electricity as about **{homes} homes**.
right.9-12: Correct: at full power all year, {mwh} MWh is about **{homes} homes'** worth of electricity.

wrong.K-2: Surprise! It uses as much electricity as about **{homes} homes**. That's a whole city!
wrong.3-5: Surprise! It uses as much electricity as about **{homes} homes**.
wrong.6-8: You picked {choice}. If it runs at full power all year, it's really about **{homes} homes**.
wrong.9-12: You picked {choice}. At full power all year, {mwh} MWh is about **{homes} homes'** worth.

text.6-8: The numbers panel shows our model's **rough estimate**. It's close to our math but not the same: real data centers don't always run at full power, and cooling uses extra electricity.
text.9-12: The panel shows our model's **rough estimate**. It differs from our full-power math because real sites don't run at 100% and cooling adds load.

text.K-2: Some data centers use **water** to cool their computers. Towns need water too!
text.3-5: Some data centers cool their computers with **water**. Towns have to make sure there's enough for everyone.

text.6-8: Some data centers cool with **water**, others mostly with air. The panel's water number is a **rough estimate**.
text.9-12: Cooling can use air or **water**. Water-cooled sites can draw heavily on a town's supply. The panel's figure is a **rough estimate**.

text.K-2: A data center can bring **jobs**. But it can also be **loud**, and it uses lots of power.
text.3-5: Data centers can bring **jobs** and **taxes** to a town. But they use lots of power, and the red circle shows where it might be **loud**.
text.6-8: Towns weigh **benefits** (jobs, tax money) against **costs** (electricity, water, noise, farmland). The red circle is a rough estimate of the loud zone.
text.9-12: Towns weigh **benefits** (tax base, jobs) against **costs** (grid load, water, noise, land use). The red circle is the model's rough loud zone.

text.K-2: Would you want a **data center** in your town?
text.3-5: Now you know a little more. Would you want a **data center** in your town?

text.6-8: Name one **good thing** and one **worry** about building it here.
text.9-12: Would you support this site? Give one **benefit** and one **cost**, using a number from this lesson.
